chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

This world appeared to ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) in the form of a blue-eyed woman. He asked her, 'How many have you married?' She said, 'Many.' He asked, 'Did you divorce them all?' She said, 'Rather, I killed them all!' He said, 'Then woe to your remaining spouses! How can they not take lesson from those who have passed?' Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said, 'The example of this world is like the salty sea – every time a thirsty person drinks from it, it increases his thirst, until it kills him.'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life / The present world
key_terms.الْبَحْرُ الْمَالِحُ: The salty sea (metaphor for insatiable desire)
key_terms.الْعَطْشَانُ: The thirsty one (metaphor for the worldly seeker)

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of the world being compared to a salty sea in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the personification of the world as a 'blue-eyed woman' highlights the seductive yet fatal nature of dunya, echoing the prophetic tradition of Jesus (AS) to warn believers against complacency. The concluding analogy of the salty sea underscores the Shia concept of *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere renunciation, but as a spiritual discipline where increased attachment leads to insatiable thirst and ultimate destruction. This serves as a practical guide for maintaining detachment while engaging with the world, ensuring one does not become consumed by it.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 9.ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “This world appeared to ʿĪsā (a) in the for of a blue-eyed woman. He asked her, ‘How many have you married?’ She said, ‘Many.’ He asked, ‘Did you divorce them all?’ She said, ‘Rather, I killed them all!’ He said, ‘Then woe to your remaining spouses! How can they not take lesson from those who have passed?’”
Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) [then] said, “The example of this world is like the salty sea – every time a thirsty person drinks from it, it increases his thirst, until it kills him.”
